Subject: MSA redlines: liability cap approach

Ben —

Thanks for sending the MSA. Attached are our redlines (ACME_Redlines_MSA_20261101.pdf). High level on the liability section: we prefer a per-order/ per-contract cap tied to the fees paid under that particular Order Form (rather than a rolling annualized cap). Our reasoning is that purchasing decisions are made per project and we need the cap to reflect the economic exposure for that specific engagement.

Key asks:
- Cap = total fees actually paid under the relevant Order Form (no multiplier).
- Carveouts: breach of confidentiality, IP indemnity, gross negligence/willful misconduct to remain uncapped.
- No annual reset — cap should be tied to the order term.

Would like to understand whether Redwood can accept per-order caps or if you require an annualized approach. Happy to hop on a quick call this week.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
VP, Procurement
Acme Analytics

Subject: RE: MSA redlines: liability cap approach — proposed language

Ben / team —

Reviewed Acme's redlines. High-level legal commercial tradeoffs below and a suggested redline snippet you can propose back to Acme:

1) Options we typically consider:
   a) Annualized cap: liability cap equals the greater of (i) fees paid to Redwood in the 12 months preceding the claim, or (ii) $250,000 (example floor). Resets annually. Pros: predictable limit aligned to spend; simpler exposure model.
   b) Per-order cap: cap equals fees paid under the relevant Order Form (no multiplier). Pros: matches Acme's ask; Cons: for multi-year orders with low up-front spend this can understate risk.
   c) Multiple-of-fees: cap = 2x or 3x fees paid (annual or per-order). This increases our exposure and is harder to accept without pricing/underwriting adjustments.

2) Carveouts we strongly recommend remain uncapped: breach of confidentiality (customer data), third-party IP indemnity, and claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct (industry standard). We should also consider excluding certain statutory liabilities where local law mandates.

3) Practical compromise (suggested):
   - Liability cap: For claims other than those in the carveouts, cap shall be the greater of (i) fees paid to Redwood under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, and (ii) $250,000.
   - For multi-year fixed-price engagements where fees in the prior 12 months are de minimis, allow parties to agree an explicit per-order cap figure in the Order Form.

Suggested redline snippet (short):
"""
Limitation of Liability. Except for (i) claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) breach of confidentiality obligations, and (iii) Redwood's indemnity obligations with respect to third-party intellectual property infringement, Redwood's liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees actually paid to Redwood under the relevant Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, and (b) Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (USD 250,000).
"""

If Acme insists on a strict per-order no-reset cap, we should seek either (i) a higher floor, or (ii) a multiplier for long-tail exposures. Happy to discuss on a quick call — attaching a short doc with the snippet for legal to push (Redwood_legal_snippet_20261102.docx).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_legal_snippet_20261102.docx (proposed redline snippet)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-analytics.com>

Subject: RE: MSA redlines: liability cap approach — proposed language

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear options. A few clarifications from Acme:

- We cannot accept an automatic annual reset. Our financial approvers require the cap to be tied to each procurement event (Order Form).
- We can accept the suggested carveouts as uncapped.
- If Redwood requires a floor, we can consider a modest fixed floor (e.g., $50k) but not one that meaningfully increases our exposure.

Counter-proposal: Liability cap = fees actually paid under the relevant Order Form, subject to a floor of Fifty Thousand Dollars (USD 50,000). Carveouts: confidentiality, IP indemnity, and willful misconduct remain uncapped.

We prefer to resolve this in writing so procurement can finalize the PO. If needed we can do a 20-minute legal-to-legal call Friday.

Best,
Elena

On a separate note, can you confirm whether Redwood's SOC 2 reports will be shared as part of the procurement packet?

Elena / team —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. After talking with legal and commercial, here's a pragmatic path that should get procurement unstuck and protect both parties:

1) Liability cap for this Order Form: the greater of (a) fees actually paid under the relevant Order Form, and (b) One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (USD 150,000). This preserves Acme's per-order linkage while giving Redwood a modest minimum.
2) Carveouts: confidentiality, IP indemnity, and claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct remain uncapped.
3) For very long-term, low-spend pilot orders we can agree to an explicit per-order cap listed on the Order Form (to avoid the prior-12-months being de minimis).

We will send a short redline back that implements the above. On SOC2: yes — we'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and evidence bundle with procurement under NDA; I'll include the HubSpot procurement ticket link here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ACME-2026-07

If that sounds acceptable I will ask Legal to issue the redline and route to you for procurement approval. Plan: Redwood legal sends updated redline on Monday and we aim to finalize before the end of next week.

Thanks,
